topic.title: The Birds That Sleep While They Fly

script.full_text: Some seabirds stay in the air for weeks, even months, without ever touching down. Which raises an impossible question: if they never land, then when on earth do they ever sleep? Scientists strapped tiny brain monitors to great frigatebirds and sent them out over the sea. The recordings revealed something remarkable: the birds really do sleep, in the air, while still soaring on the wind. They sleep in tiny bursts of just seconds, often resting only half the brain at a time while the other half stays alert. Sometimes, riding a rising current, they even shut down both halves at once. In a whole month at sea, they sleep barely forty minutes a day, a fraction of what they take on land. High above the waves, these birds have quietly mastered a trick that still leaves scientists amazed.
